text_blocks.snippet: Treatment options for high blood pressure (hypertension) include lifestyle changes and prescription medications tailored to your blood pressure level and overall health.
snippet_highlighted_words: lifestyle changes and prescription medications tailored to your blood pressure level and overall health

list.snippet: Dietary changes: Follow a heart-healthy plan like the DASH diet, which focuses on fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy while cutting back on sodium (salt).
Physical activity: Get at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise, such as brisk walking, each week.
Weight management: Lose excess weight and maintain a healthy body weight to reduce strain on your heart and blood vessels.
Habits: Limit alcohol intake, avoid tobacco products, manage stress, and get adequate sleep.

text_blocks.snippet: If lifestyle adjustments alone do not lower your numbers enough, doctors often prescribe one or more of these first-line drug classes:

list.snippet: ARBs (Angiotensin Receptor Blockers): Help keep blood vessels relaxed by blocking a hormone that makes them constrict (e.g., losartan, valsartan).
ACE Inhibitors: Help relax and widen blood vessels by blocking the formation of narrowing chemicals (e.g., lisinopril, enalapril).
Calcium Channel Blockers: Prevent calcium from entering heart and vessel muscle cells to let arteries widen (e.g., amlodipine, nifedipine).
Thiazide Diuretics: Water pills that help your body get rid of extra sodium and water (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide, chlorthalidone).

text_blocks.snippet: For more details, you can review the Mayo Clinic High Blood Pressure Guide or the NIH Treatment Overview.
